title: test_mac.rs: HMAC and CMAC via digest::Mac (PR #10305)
description:
Write tests/test_mac.rs: test digest::Mac impls for CMAC (AES-128/192/256) and HMAC (all SHA variants) against NIST SP 800-38B and Wycheproof JSON.

## What
Verify MAC trait impls (PR #10305) produce byte-exact output and reject wrong tags, using full coverage across key sizes and message lengths that the PR itself omits.

## Algorithm
1. CMAC tests (from testvectors/nist/cmac_38b.rs):
   a. For each key_size in [128, 192, 256] and each of 4 message lengths (0, 16, 40, 64 bytes):
   b. use digest::Mac; let mut mac = CmacAes128::new_from_slice(key).unwrap();
   c. Mac::update(&mut mac, msg); let tag = mac.finalize_fixed();
   d. assert_eq!(tag.as_slice(), expected, 'CMAC AES-{} Mlen={} failed');
   e. Negative: CmacAes128::new_from_slice(key).unwrap().verify_slice(msg, &wrong_tag) returns Err.
2. HMAC tests (from Wycheproof JSON):
   For each variant in [sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha512_224, sha512_256, sha3_224, sha3_256, sha3_384, sha3_512]:
   a. load external/wycheproof/testvectors_v1/hmac_{variant}_test.json
   b. For each valid case: HmacSha256::new_from_slice(key).unwrap().chain_update(msg).finalize_fixed() == expected_tag
   c. For each invalid case: verify_slice returns Err
3. Compile-time checks: fn _mac<M: digest::Mac>() {} for Cmac* and Hmac* types.

## Defensive rules
- If a Wycheproof file does not exist (setup.sh not run), panic with a clear message pointing to setup.sh — do not silently skip
- CMAC AES-192 and AES-256: if these types do not exist in PR #10305, document with compile_fail; do not skip silently
- Key material (HMAC key) must never appear in assert_eq! failure message (use assert_mac_eq! helper from common.rs that redacts key)

## Agent team
- Agent R: read PR #10305 cmac_mac.rs and hmac_mac.rs to confirm exact type names (CmacAes128? Cmac<Aes128>?) and feature flags
- Agent I: write test_mac.rs per algorithm above
- Agent T: independently transcribe NIST SP 800-38B D.1 Example 1 (AES-128, 0-byte msg, key=2b7e..., tag=bb1d6929e95937287fa37d129b756746); verify vs cmac_38b.rs constant

## Tests (oracles)
- CMAC AES-128 Mlen=0: oracle = NIST SP 800-38B D.1 Ex.1 = bb1d6929e95937287fa37d129b756746
- CMAC AES-128 Mlen=16: oracle = NIST SP 800-38B D.1 Ex.2 = 070a16b46b4d4144f79bdd9dd04a287c
- CMAC AES-192 all 4 lengths: oracle = NIST SP 800-38B D.2 (NOT tested in PR #10305)
- HMAC-SHA-256: Wycheproof hmac_sha256_test.json (superset of RFC 4231; PR only tests 3 of ~100 cases)
